title: Design: Picking a customer in the chip keeps the table headings in place
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, the asset's current owner.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B, a payer.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer C, the asset's earlier owner.
  • Have a new asset for this test, asset 1, now owned by customer A, that earlier belonged to customer C, with work order 1 for customer C billing itself (made first, while customer C owned it) and work order 2 for customer A billed to customer B (made later), both at the test location.
  • Open the attached pictures bt-p7-02-after-whole-history.png, bt-p7-04-after-one-customer-picked.png, bt-p7-10-after-work-orders-tab-top.png at 100% zoom beside the screen.
custom_steps:
1. Open asset 1's Work Orders tab from customer A's page.
  2. Take a screenshot of the page.
  3. Click the "Customer" filter chip.
  4. Tick customer C.
  5. Click outside the panel.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 and work order 2 are listed; a "Bill To" column reads customer B's name on work order 2 and is blank on work order 1.

Step 2:

  • You have a picture of where each heading, field and button sits before the change.

Step 3:

  • The panel opens.

Step 4:

  • Customer C is ticked.

Step 5:

  • Only work order 1 is listed.
  • The "Bill To" column still shows, blank on work order 1.
  • Every column heading of the table is in the same place as in your screenshot: none has moved left or right (the chip itself now shows customer C's name).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Bill To", Confluence 1003585538, version 0.5 (6 Nov 2026, pending approval, Chris Ward), read 9 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-12289, story SV-12316 (Story 14, Asset Work Orders tab: whole history and Customer filter)

  • S14-R6: “A "Bill To" column shows when at least one row bills someone else; it is blank on self-billed rows.”
  • S14-R4: “The filter is multi-select; a work order matches when a picked customer is its customer or its Bill To.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Bill To design" (https://claude.ai/artifact/2prSHgwt2tWCz96QD2DWkd), version 1794510417-a68d (its boards are byte-identical to version 1794239066-4906 read 9 Nov 2026), read 13 Nov 2026: pictures "Whole history" (page 7 "Asset Work Orders tab", This build), "One customer picked" (page 7 "Asset Work Orders tab", New, no before exists), "Work Orders tab, top" (page 7 "Asset Work Orders tab", This build). Compare the screen with the pictures; the expected results come from the PRD.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • bt-p7-02-after-whole-history.png
  • bt-p7-04-after-one-customer-picked.png
  • bt-p7-10-after-work-orders-tab-top.png

The design's own words:

  • “Every work order on the asset at this location, for every owner and payer, oldest first as today: Kolosov's work orders now appear too.”
  • “Quartzsite ticked: "1 selected", and the chip reads "Customer: Quartzsite Truc...".”
  • “A "Bill To" column sits right after Customer because a loaded row bills someone else. S2-17579 reads "Buda Truck Repair", "Valders Diesel & Fleet Repair".”

The PRD's column rule does not say whether it counts the rows before or after a filter; the design draws no filtered list with the column, and its pictures with and without the column place the later headings 77 to 213 pixels apart. These results follow the suggested answer of question 17.
